title: Media Converter input

url.title: Media URL
url.description: Direct, publicly downloadable URL of ONE audio or video file (http/https; redirects followed). Any FFmpeg-readable format: mp4, mov, mkv, webm, avi, mp3, wav, m4a, ogg, flac, opus... Max 2 GB. Must be the file itself, not a YouTube/web page. Example: https://download.samplelib.com/mp4/sample-5s.mp4

target.title: Target format
target.description: Output format, applied to `url` and to any `files` item without its own target. Default: mp3. Audio: mp3 (VBR ~190 kbps), wav (16-bit PCM, original rate), wav16k (mono, 16 000 Hz, 16-bit PCM - use this before Whisper/speech-to-text), flac (lossless), ogg (Vorbis), m4a (AAC 192 kbps). Video: mp4 (H.264 + AAC, web/faststart), webm (VP9 + Opus). Image: gif (animated, 8 fps, 360 px wide, no audio), thumbnail (single JPEG frame at startSeconds, default first frame). Audio targets need an input audio stream; video/gif/thumbnail need a video stream.

startSeconds.title: Start at (seconds)
startSeconds.description: Optional trim start in whole seconds from the beginning of the input, e.g. 30. For target=thumbnail this is the frame time (default: first frame). Applies to `url` and acts as the default for every `files` item; a `files` item's own startSeconds overrides it (and may be fractional, e.g. 12.5).

durationSeconds.title: Duration (seconds)
durationSeconds.description: Optional length in whole seconds to keep from startSeconds, e.g. 600 for 10 minutes. Billing is per started minute of OUTPUT, so trimming lowers cost; also lets inputs longer than maxDurationSeconds be processed. Applies to `url` and is the default for every `files` item; per-item durationSeconds overrides it.

files.title: Batch of files
files.description: Optional batch, processed sequentially. Array of objects: {"url": string (required), "target": one of the target values (optional, falls back to top-level target), "startSeconds": number (optional, seconds from start to begin, e.g. 30; falls back to top-level startSeconds), "durationSeconds": number (optional, seconds to keep, e.g. 60; falls back to top-level durationSeconds)}. Example: [{"url":"https://example.com/talk.mp4","target":"wav16k"},{"url":"https://example.com/clip.mov","target":"gif","startSeconds":5,"durationSeconds":4}]. Plain URL strings are also accepted. Failed items return status=error and are not charged.

maxDurationSeconds.title: Max input duration (s)
maxDurationSeconds.description: Safety cap in seconds on input duration (default 10800 = 3 hours). Longer inputs are rejected with status=error (not charged) unless durationSeconds is set (top-level or on the item) to trim. Billing is per started minute of OUTPUT, so trimming also lowers cost.

description: Convert one or more public audio/video URLs with FFmpeg. Pass either `url` (+ `target`) for a single file, or `files` for a batch. Each output file is returned as a download URL in the dataset.
